A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures and appendices A–H. Renumbered theorems and relocated experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original Gaussian-mixture classification experiments, with experimental details in Appendix H.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H report original experiments, including new transformer comparisons and norm/covariance shift results.

M1.justification: The proposed sparse single-layer linear-attention transformer, sigmoid/softmax outputs, label-sampling procedures and training objectives in Sections 3–4 are retained. The new encoder architecture serves as an experimental comparator.

E1.justification: V2 adds unequal-component-norm and multiple-covariance pretraining scenarios, evaluated against the original fixed-covariance, equal-norm setting (Section 5.1). This expands distributional coverage within the retained synthetic Gaussian-mixture classification task.

E2.justification: V1’s three-layer GPT-2 comparator is replaced by an encoder-only softmax transformer without positional encoding (v2 Figure 3 and Appendix H.2). V2 also introduces single-layer versus three-layer comparisons into the scaling experiments. The full single-layer transformer, softmax regression, linear/Gaussian SVMs, 1-NN and 3-NN remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds 100,000-task Adam training protocols for its scaling and distribution-shift comparisons. Figure 1 introduces sweeps including N = 10, 20, 40 and M = 5–60. The original 10,000-task SGD scaling experiments remain in Figure 4. The deep comparator also changes from a decoder with loss over positions 41–101 to an encoder without positional encoding.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 2 directly tests unequal mean norms and varying training covariances, comparing their effects on single-layer and three-layer models. These substantially extend v1’s prompt-length/class-count analyses and analytical discussion of assumption violations. V2 also extends scaling analyses to the deeper model; the original analyses are retained in Appendix H.

E5.justification: V2 retains ten random-seed repetitions for the original scaling study and three for the general comparison, and reports three for its new studies. However, it removes v1 Appendix H’s explicit identification of plotted results and uncertainty bands as means and standard deviations, although shaded bands remain.

E6.justification: V2 adds scaling comparisons and norm/covariance robustness results. The substituted encoder’s error decreases beyond M = 100, unlike v1’s GPT-2 curve; at M = 140 their respective plotted errors are approximately 0.05 and 0.11. These are results for different architectures. V2 Figure 4 reproduces v1 Figure 1’s results unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 omits the explicit condition 0 < alpha from the main convergence statements’ Equations (9) and (18), although positivity remains in the appendix arguments and formal multiclass theorem. Otherwise, the distributional assumptions, convergence rates, inference bounds and proof arguments are retained after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and third contribution replace convergence to a Bayes-optimal classifier with convergence to the ground-truth label distribution. This refines an existing central claim while retaining the training-convergence and prompt-length guarantees. The older Bayes-optimal wording persists in Appendix H.1.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new experiments as showing behavioral similarities between shallow linear and deeper nonlinear transformers, alongside greater robustness of the latter to distribution changes. It removes v1 Section 5.2’s explanation of GPT-2’s long-prompt deterioration after replacing that comparator, substantially revising the empirical applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix H.2 documents the x-transformers encoder, absence of positional encoding, and training settings and generators for the new experiments; the GPT-2 implementation and loss discussion are removed. The new covariance specification is inconsistent: Figure 2’s caption uses absolute N(3,1) diagonal entries, whereas Appendix H.2 specifies additional matrices with half their entries 0.1 and half 100.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bu et al. (2024), Hahn and Goyal (2023), Li et al. (2024b), and Lin and Lee (2024), extending distinctions from idealized next-token predictors and earlier binary-classification training analyses. It removes the Radford and Wolf references associated with GPT-2/HuggingFace. The central novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 specifies Gaussian mixtures in the title, updates author affiliations, edits introduction and explanatory paragraphs, and renumbers theoretical statements. It reorganizes Section 5 and Appendix H, moving the original single-layer experimental discussion to H.1. Most method and proof prose remains stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds two-panel scaling-comparison and robustness figures, enlarges and relabels the general comparison plot, and moves the original four-panel Figure 1 to Appendix Figure 4. This substantially reorganizes the experimental displays; the relocated four panel images themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns its headline inference claim with the distribution matching established in Sections 3–4 and adds useful empirical evidence about assumption sensitivity and deeper transformers. These gains are limited by conflicting covariance specifications, removal of the uncertainty-band explanation, and residual Bayes-optimal wording in Appendix H.1. The result is a modest net improvement in clarity and empirical support.
